steps: Never put batteries in regular or wet waste: they can leak toxins and start fires.
Tape the terminals of lithium and button cells before storing them.
Keep them in a dry container until you can hand them to an e-waste or battery collection point.
battery.tip: Many electronics shops and e-waste collectors accept used batteries.

steps: Put food scraps, peels and garden waste in the wet-waste bin.
Drain excess liquid and keep it separate from dry recyclables.
Home composting is ideal if you have the space.
biological.tip: Do not mix wet waste with plastic bags unless the bag is compostable.

steps: Empty and rinse the bottle or jar.
Remove caps and lids and recycle them separately.
Keep brown glass apart from ceramics, mirrors and bulbs, which are not recyclable with bottle glass.
brown-glass.tip: Handle broken glass carefully: wrap it in paper before disposal.

steps: Remove tape, labels and packing material.
Flatten boxes to save space.
Keep cardboard dry; food-soiled or greasy parts cannot be recycled.
cardboard.tip: Cut greasy sections off pizza boxes and recycle only the clean part.

steps: Wearable clothes: wash and donate them to a charity or clothing drive.
Worn-out textiles: give them to a textile recycler or reuse them as cleaning rags.
Heavily soiled or wet items go with general (reject) waste.
clothes.tip: Repairing or upcycling clothes is the most eco-friendly option.

steps: Empty and rinse the bottle or jar.
Remove caps and lids and recycle them separately.
Keep green glass apart from ceramics, mirrors and bulbs, which are not recyclable with bottle glass.
green-glass.tip: Handle broken glass carefully: wrap it in paper before disposal.

steps: Empty and rinse cans and tins.
Crush them if possible to save space.
Only put aerosol cans in the bin when they are completely empty.
metal.tip: Larger scrap metal can be sold to a scrap dealer.

steps: Keep paper clean and dry.
Remove plastic covers, spiral bindings and metal clips where possible.
Used tissues, greasy paper and waxed paper are not recyclable.
paper.tip: Shredded paper is better bagged separately so it does not scatter.

steps: Empty, rinse and dry bottles and containers.
Check the recycling number on the item; local acceptance varies.
Thin films and wrappers are often not accepted, so check local rules.
plastic.tip: Reducing single-use plastic matters more than recycling it.

shoes.bin: Reuse / donate, else dry reject waste
steps: Wearable shoes: clean them and donate them in pairs.
Repair worn shoes at a cobbler when possible.
Beyond repair: dispose of them as dry reject waste or at a shoe-recycling drop-off if one exists near you.
shoes.tip: Tie pairs together so they stay matched when donated.

steps: Place non-recyclable items in the general waste bin.
Double-check whether part of the item is recyclable before throwing it away.
Never dispose of hazardous items such as batteries, bulbs or chemicals here.
trash.tip: If unsure, check your local municipality's segregation guidelines.

steps: Empty and rinse the bottle or jar.
Remove caps and lids and recycle them separately.
Keep clear glass apart from ceramics, mirrors and bulbs, which are not recyclable with bottle glass.
white-glass.tip: Handle broken glass carefully: wrap it in paper before disposal.
